title: Placebo ESP experiments: data and code
description:
Hit counts for every experiment in a set of placebo ESP experiments run between 2006 and 2013, in which random numbers stood in for both the target and the guess, so that no psi was possible. The main series is 38,016,682 experiments of Spencer-Brown's morning-afternoon design (about 19 billion binary trials) using atmospheric-noise random numbers from random.org. Smaller series used a pseudo-random generator (the Mersenne Twister in R), a hardware generator (Simtec Electronics' Entropy Key), Spencer-Brown's digit-matching design (random.org and Entropy Key) and Zener cards (473,594 experiments of 625 trials).

The deposit includes the code that recovered the counts from the original R workspaces, the code for every table and figure in Anomalous Significance Revisited: Nineteen Billion Placebo Trials and the Normal Approximation and Too Many Miracles, a simulation of the Iversen et al. (1971) test battery with the result for every simulated data set, the whole data set as one R file (data/placebo_esp.RData), a script that rebuilds every experiment of the main series from random.org's public archive of the original daily files (all 38,016,682 rebuilt exactly), and tests of dependence between successive bits in the 19,008,341,000 bits the main series used. Code is under the MIT licence; data and results are under CC BY 4.0.
